documents.unit: Library research guide, section by Center for Educational Effectiveness
documents.title: Generative AI for Teaching, Research and Learning: Teaching and Learning
documents.summary: A library-hosted guide section written by the Center for Educational Effectiveness. It gives advice rather than rules: students check each instructor's policy and use AI to support their thinking, and instructors get links to syllabus examples and consultations.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule of its own: it says "policies regarding Generative AI may vary from instructor to instructor" and tells students to "check with their instructors", so the decision is handed to instructors.

units.why: "students should always check with their instructors" tells students to ask first; P10 fits better than P78 because the emphasis is checking before use.
units.anchor: students should always check with their instructors

units.why: "Policies regarding Generative AI may vary from instructor to instructor" says the rule is set per instructor; P04 fits.
units.anchor: policies regarding Generative AI may vary from instructor to instructor

units.why: "Generative AI should be used to support and enhance your thinking" says AI must not replace the student's thinking; P32 fits better than P12 because it is about the student staying the thinker.
units.anchor: Generative AI should be used to support and enhance your thinking

units.why: "Always be mindful of the risks and limitations of Generative AI tools" asks students to stay aware of tool limits; P31 is nearest though it does not say to verify.
units.anchor: Always be mindful of the risks and limitations of Generative AI tools
units.fit_note: Asks for mindfulness of risks and limitations generally, not explicitly for verifying output.

units.why: "Engage with Generative AI output critically" asks students to evaluate output, which is P31.
units.anchor: Engage with Generative AI output critically and practice information literacy

units.why: "Always follow academic integrity guidelines and instructor policies regarding Generative AI" makes students responsible for following the rules that apply; P78 fits, not P36 because misconduct classification is not stated.
units.anchor: Always follow academic integrity guidelines and instructor policies regarding Generative AI

units.why: "Practice proper citation practices for Generative AI use" asks students to cite AI use, which is P24.
units.anchor: Practice proper citation practices for Generative AI use

units.why: CEE says it "provides a number of resources, events, and consultations" on AI and teaching, which supports faculty learning (P63).
units.anchor: provides a number of resources, events, and consultations related to Generative AI and teaching

units.why: CEE experts "are available to help instructors explore teaching strategies and construct course policies"; this is faculty support (P63).
units.anchor: available to help instructors explore teaching strategies and construct course policies pertaining to Generative AI

units.why: The guide lists examples to help instructors "develop transparent expectations and policies"; nearest is P09 but it is not a mandate.
units.anchor: develop transparent expectations and policies regarding Generative AI in their courses
units.fit_note: Offers syllabus-language examples to develop transparent expectations; does not require a syllabus statement.

units.why: "Instructors may benefit from exploring ways to intentionally incorporate AI into their course materials" encourages instructors to use AI in teaching; P59 is nearest.
units.anchor: Instructors may benefit from exploring ways to intentionally incorporate AI into their course materials
units.fit_note: Concerns incorporating AI into course materials and instruction, not drafting teaching documents.

units.why: AI tools are "quite useful for personalizing learning experiences", naming a benefit (P87).
units.anchor: quite useful for personalizing learning experiences and rethinking teaching and instruction

units.why: "both students and instructors should carefully consider the limitations and emerging best practices" asks all users to stay informed; P102.
units.anchor: both students and instructors should carefully consider the limitations and emerging best practices

units.why: The guide says AI "has disrupted established teaching strategies" and raises open questions about protecting learning; it states no rule, so UNCOVERED rather than a stretched fit.
units.anchor: Generative AI has disrupted established teaching strategies for many instructors
units.uncovered_note: Acknowledges that AI has disrupted teaching and raises open questions about protecting student learning.

units.why: "scholarly research has only just begun to explore the implications" says evidence on AI and learning is thin; P55 is nearest.
units.anchor: scholarly research has only just begun to explore the implications of Generative AI
units.fit_note: States that evidence is still emerging rather than collecting or citing it.

units.why: Early scholarship is cited as suggesting "intentional and critical use of Generative AI can support student learning", citing evidence (P55) and favoring critical use.
units.anchor: intentional and critical use of Generative AI can support student learning

notes: Only one included document; the Code of Academic Conduct and IET pages were not fetched (Cloudflare block), so the university layer is thin.
